newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices slip back to flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices slip back to flat.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds late Thursday edged down to unchanged, with a softer bias, as the market's continued its move lower after the Federal Reserve Chairman suggested he would act swiftly to arrest inflation.
Alan Greenspan on Wednesday warned that he was prepared to act pre-emptively to prevent inflation from taking root and questioned whether the equities market could sustain its gains.
The big drop in 30-year Treasury bonds, which boosted yields by about 14 basis points from late Tuesday, helped bring individual investors back to the municipal market, however.

"We had a fantastic retail day," said a trader. "But then looking out at the Street, it seems like there's a lot of volatility out there in 'Muniland'....We saw a lot of big money orders come in, probably much more so than in the past few days, probably because of the reaction to the big price drop."
Yield-sensitive retail invstors for most of the past 12-months have pumped their money into equities at the expense of the municipal market.
Despite the fixed income market's strong retreat, which led several issuers to postpone offerings, traders largely shrugged off concerns about several of the key sales priced over the past two days.
For example, the Municipal Assistance Corporation for New York City's $465 million offering, which some had feared was priced too richly, now appeared to have done well despite the difficult market.
"I think the MAC deal is in good shape," said a trader.

The MAC bonds were repriced on Thursday, with the yield on the 2008 maturity raised five basis points to 5.05 percent, and some traders said that it was not uncommon for the offering commanded a premium over a sale of $259 million of bonds by the New York Thruway Authority. Those bonds commanded a 5.58 percent yield in 2017.
Still, Maryland's offering of $240 million of general obligation bonds, which fetched a top yield of 5.0 percent in 2008, late Thursday had a nearly $78 million balance.

And the supply of new bonds for next week is expected to fall off from the $3.4 billion total slated for this week. Municipal bond sales for next week are expected to total $1.9 billion in 62 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $1.2 billion in 23 sales, with a $300 million Jefferson County, Ala., issue through Raymond James topping the list.
On the competitive side, 39 sales totaling $744 million are on the schedule. A $450 million North Carolina deal on Wednesday is the largest.

U.S. Treasury bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade fell four ticks to 110-24/32, while the March municipal bond futures rose one tick to 115-26/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 162 ticks.
In the secondary market, Florida Ports Financing Revenues of June 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were offered at 5.80 percent, NET, up five basis points.
And Ohio State Turnpike Revenues of February 2026, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were offered at 98-1/4, down 1/2 of a point.
